title: Navigation
description: Recursive sidebar navigation with capability-prune, drill-down screens, and group/separator items.

documentation.purpose: Menu host + renderer dispatcher. Reads the resolved `menu` tree from the kernel config (nested entries, screen-bound by the PHP `bind_screens` pass), orders + prunes it once (sort by `position`; recursively drop hidden, capability-denied, and orphan-separator items), then dispatches to the renderer the active engine named via its `engine.json` `menu-renderer` field (threaded onto the runtime config by `buildRuntimeConfig`). Dispatch goes through the kernel menu-renderer registry (`src/runtime/config/menuRendererRegistry.js`), so a `plugin:*` renderer resolves by the same path as a built-in. Ships two renderers — `sidebar-drilldown` (default; slide-in sub-screens + `?screen=<id>` URL slot, honors `config.collapsed` icon rail) and `sidebar-tree` (expandable in-place tree). `core:single-pane`'s `drawer` renderer registers from that engine's module. `menu-renderer: none` → renders nothing; absent → falls back to `sidebar-drilldown`. Active state derives from the URL primary path via `aria-current="true"`.

reads.purpose: `useKernel().config` supplies the resolved `menu` tree to order/prune and the engine's `menu-renderer` strategy id to dispatch on.
Decode site title for the root drill-down screen heading.

Per-item capability check via the kernel's `userCan(cap)` helper. Reads a sync cache populated by an `api-fetch` REST call. Items declaring `capability` get pruned recursively when the user lacks the cap.

states.renders: Nothing. Engine drives navigation through `regions` / `routes` instead.
Expandable in-place tree; branch nodes are <button>s with a rotating chevron, leaves are links. Branches seed open when their subtree contains the active route.
Vertical column of IconButton entries; separators render as <hr>; external links render as native <a target="_blank">.
Sidebar drill-down `screen` showing the root item list. Title falls back to admin.json `title` → `record.title` → window global → `Admin`.
Drill-down sub-screen with back button + screen.label heading + screen.description + items list.

interactions.effect: `navigateScreen(item.screen)` writes `?screen=<id>` to the URL on top of the current primary path; SidebarNavigationProvider plays a slide animation.
`navigateScreen(null)` clears the slot; slide animation reverses.
Plain anchor navigation via `<a href>` — the kernel router intercepts in-shell hrefs (starting with `#`).
Native browser behavior — opens in new tab. Items render as `<a>` (via `render` prop) so this works.

a11y.focus-management: Drill-down's `SidebarContent` restores focus after back navigation to the screen item that opened it.
a11y.screen-reader: Active item carries `aria-current="true"`. Items render as `<a>` (not `<button>`) when `href` is set so screen readers announce links, not buttons. The region wrapper already provides the `navigation` landmark — the app does NOT add its own `<nav>`.

constraints.note: Sub-screen state is `?screen=<id>` in the URL, not `useState`. Deep-links + refresh survive. Multiple sidebars in one shell would collide on the slot — namespace later (`?nav-{regionId}-screen=…`) if needed.
Active state lives on `aria-current="true"` only — no `.is-active` class. CSS targets the attribute; the redundant class would cause drift.

Sidebar internals mirror `@wordpress/edit-site/src/components/sidebar*` BEM naming — `wp-admin-workspaces-sidebar-navigation-{screen,item}`. Keep one-for-one with edit-site so its source is the structural reference.
WPDS IconButton wraps Base UI Button which always renders a native `<button>` and silently drops `href`. We use `render={<a href={...}/>}` to swap the element.
SidebarNavigationItem only sets `aria-current`; legacy `.is-active` is intentionally absent.
`pruneNavItems` recursively walks the tree. A screen/group whose children all prune renders nothing (the screen itself drops). Orphan separators at top/bottom are stripped.
Uses legacy `__experimentalItemGroup` from `@wordpress/components` — WPDS 0.12 has no port.
Region wrapper renders `<div role="navigation">`; the app must NOT nest its own `<nav>` (would double the landmark).

WP-admin ships an unlayered `a { color: var(--wp-admin-theme-color) }` rule that wins against `@wordpress/ui` Button's layered color. The bundled `core:default` engine ships a defensive unlayered `.wp-admin-workspaces-region--sidebar a { color: var(--wpds-color-fg-interactive-neutral) }` rule (+ `:hover/:focus/:active` variants). A non-WPDS engine MUST emit an equivalent unlayered rule for whatever color scheme its chrome uses, or anchor-rendered nav buttons will inherit wp-admin's blue.

`@wordpress/icons` SVGs do not set `fill`, so library icons paint browser-default black. The bundled `core:default` engine ships `.wp-admin-workspaces-region--sidebar svg { fill: currentColor }`. A non-WPDS engine MUST force `fill: currentColor` on the icons it pairs with this app or icons render in the wrong color.

`@wordpress/ui` Stack's `display: flex` rule lives in `@layer wp-ui-components` and loses against unlayered WP-admin CSS. The bundled `core:default` engine ships an unlayered `.wp-admin-workspaces [class*="__stack"] { display: flex }` defensive rule. A rebuild that uses Stack-style flex containers must defeat unlayered host CSS the same way (or use a non-layered layout primitive).

design-system-leakage.purpose: Item icons + nav list — WPDS 0.12 gaps.
Reads `root/site.title` for the root drill-down screen heading.
Decodes HTML entities in the site title before rendering.
Icon names from admin.json resolve through the kernel icon registry — bundled `core:default` engine ships the `@wordpress/icons` table.
